rules.coverage_text: Rental properties in Los Angeles that were first built on or before October 1, 1978.
rules.quote: Effective March 30, 2020, through January 31, 2024, rent increases are prohibited for rental units subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO).
rules.requirement: Rent increases are prohibited for RSO-covered units from March 30, 2020 through January 31, 2024.
rules.title: Rent Increase Prohibition Period

rules.coverage_text: Rental properties in Los Angeles that were first built on or before October 1, 1978.
rules.quote: Rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage (click here to view the allowable rent increase PDF). Effective February 2, 2026, the landlord can no longer include an additional percentage increase for utilities.
rules.requirement: Landlords may increase rent once per 12-month period by the allowable rent increase percentage set by the city, without additional increases for utilities as of February 2, 2026.
rules.title: Annual Rent Increase Allowance

rules.coverage_text: Rental properties in Los Angeles that were first built on or before October 1, 1978.

key_values.name: Notice Period for Additional Tenant
key_values.text: within 60 days of learning about the additional tenant

rules.quote: Effective February 2, 2026, an additonal 10% increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy is no longer permitted. However, a 10% for an additional tenant is allowed (not a dependent) if moves into a rental unit: Landlords can increase the rent within 60 days of learning about the additional tenant.
rules.requirement: As of February 2, 2026, landlords may no longer collect a 10% increase for additional dependents, but may collect a 10% increase for an additional (non-dependent) tenant, with written notice within 60 days of learning about the additional tenant.
rules.title: Additional Tenant Rent Increase

rules.coverage_text: Rental properties in Los Angeles that were first built on or before October 1, 1978.
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay interest on security deposits held by tenants in RSO-covered units.
rules.title: Security Deposit Interest

rules.coverage_text: Rental properties in Los Angeles that were first built on or before October 1, 1978.
rules.quote: Legal Reasons for Eviction Tenant is at-fault Failure to pay rent Failure to fix or address a violation of the rental agreement Creating a nuisance or causing damage to the rental unit Using the rental unit for an illegal purpose Failure to renew a similar rental agreement Failure to provide the landlord with reasonable access to the rental unit The person at the end of the lease term is a subtenant not approved by the landlord Tenant is not at-fault The owner or immediate family member will move into the rental unit A resident manager will move into the rental unit Demolition and permanent removal from the rental market Government order Conversion to affordable housing
rules.requirement: Evictions under the RSO must be for legal reasons specified in the ordinance, including both at-fault reasons (failure to pay rent, lease violations, nuisance, illegal use, failure to renew, denied access, unapproved subtenant) and no-fault reasons (owner occupancy, manager occupancy, demolition, government order, conversion to affordable housing).
rules.title: Legal Reasons for Eviction

rules.coverage_text: Rental properties in Los Angeles that were first built on or before October 1, 1978.

key_values.name: Filing Deadline
key_values.text: within three (3) business days of service on the tenant

rules.quote: All notices to terminate a tenancy for all rental units subject to City's Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) must be filed with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) within three (3) business days of service on the tenant per Los Angeles Municipal Code 151.09.C.9 & 165.05.B.5.
rules.requirement: Landlords must file all eviction notices with LAHD within three business days of serving the tenant.
rules.title: Eviction Notice Filing Requirement

rules.coverage_text: Rental properties in Los Angeles that were first built on or before October 1, 1978.
rules.quote: A $1.61 monthly surcharge may be collected by the landlord as the tenant's portion of the Registration fee. Effective January 1, 2020, the surcharge is $38.75.
rules.requirement: Landlords may collect a monthly surcharge from tenants for the rental registration fee, which is $38.75 per month effective January 1, 2020.
rules.title: Registration Fee Surcharge

rules.coverage_text: Rental properties in Los Angeles that were first built on or before October 1, 1978.
rules.quote: Effective January 1, 2022, a landlord may collect 1/12 of 50% of the annual Systematic Code Enforcement Fee from the tenant of the rental unit per month.
rules.requirement: Landlords may collect from tenants a monthly surcharge equal to 1/12 of 50% of the annual Systematic Code Enforcement Fee, effective January 1, 2022.
rules.title: Systematic Code Enforcement Fee Pass-Through

rules.coverage_text: Rental properties in Los Angeles that were first built on or before October 1, 1978.
rules.quote: A $3.00 surcharge may be added to the rent for the installation and cost of a hard-wired smoke detector or a combination smoke/ carbon monoxide detector.
rules.requirement: Landlords may collect a $3.00 monthly surcharge for the installation and cost of hard-wired smoke detectors or combination smoke/carbon monoxide detectors.
rules.title: Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Detector Surcharge
